title: Appendix A.4 applied to density thresholds of a rescaling- and tangent-closed class of measures (conditional on the abstract dimension reduction theorem) (with the density semicontinuity lemma proved inside)
statement: Assume (ADR): the abstract dimension reduction theorem (Simon Appendix A.4 with (H0)), in exactly the form of the frozen Lean type of Submission.abstract_dimension_reduction. That is: for all P′, n′, Q′ ∈ ℕ, every set F of functions ℝ^{P′} → ℝ^{Q′} and every map sing satisfying (H0), local μH[n′]-integrability, A.1, A.2 and A.3 (closedness, emptiness for flat indicators of n′-planes, rescaling, and the ε-neighbourhood semicontinuity), either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for all φ ∈ F, or (II) there is d with d + 1 ≤ n′ such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for all φ ∈ F and α > 0, some ψ ∈ F and a d-dimensional subspace L have sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L and λ > 0, and, if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for all φ ∈ F and σ < 1. Under (ADR): Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, c > 0, Λ ∈ ℝ, and let 𝓜 be a set of Borel measures on ℝ^P. For a measure μ and x ∈ ℝ^P let dens μ x := (limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ)).toReal (limsup in [0, ∞], ω_n = unitBallVolume n; toReal sends ∞ to 0). For y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 put μ^{y,λ} := ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ) • μ.map (dilation y λ) (= λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ). Assume: (1) every μ ∈ 𝓜 is finite on compact sets; (2) every μ ∈ 𝓜 equals Hⁿ.withDensity (ofReal ∘ dens μ), Hⁿ = μHE[n]; (3) μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 whenever μ ∈ 𝓜, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; (4) for μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0, there are a strictly increasing sub : ℕ → ℕ and ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(λ·s) = λⁿν(s) for all λ > 0 and Borel s, and ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ; (5) for μ ∈ 𝓜 and y, R with B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0), ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·μ(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (6) there is no μ ∈ 𝓜 with μ(ℝ^P) = ∞ and dens μ = c′·1_Q (pointwise) for some n-dimensional linear subspace Q and some real c′ ≥ c. Then either (I) for every μ ∈ 𝓜 the set {x ∈ B_1(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} is empty; or (II) there is d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 ≤ n such that μH[d + α]({x ∈ B_1(0) : c ≤ dens μ x}) = 0 for all μ ∈ 𝓜 and real α > 0; if d = 0, {x ∈ B_σ(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} is finite for all μ ∈ 𝓜 and σ < 1; and there are ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(ℝ^P) = ∞ and a linear subspace L with dim L = d, {x : c ≤ dens ν x} = L and dens ν (y + λx) = dens ν x for all y ∈ L, λ > 0 and x. (In the Lean statement dens is a universally quantified function fixed by its defining equation.)
